h: Getting There and Making a Day of It
p: Cambuslang sits on the south-east edge of Glasgow, which makes it easy to reach from across the city and from Lanarkshire. It has its own railway station with regular trains into Glasgow Central, so groups can get there without needing a designated driver.

For petrolheads, a trip to the Riverside Museum is the obvious companion to a race. It's Glasgow's free museum of transport and travel, on the banks of the Clyde, with vintage cars, trams, locomotives and a recreated old street. The building itself, with its zigzag roof, is a sight to see.
Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum is another free favourite, and the Glasgow Science Centre is a strong option for families with curious kids.
Arrive a bit early so the whole crew is through sign-in together and nobody misses the briefing.

On the karting side, the drivers who do best are the ones who stay calm under pressure. Hold your line, brake before the bend and don't let the kart behind you rattle you. The lap times always tell the truth in the end, so drive your own race and the results will follow. Book ahead for weekends, and remember that football days at Hampden can make the roads around the south side a bit busier.
